proposal.summary: The ashmem mmap implementation stores the backing shmem file in vm_file without enforcing ashmem's protection mask on that file's ->mmap(), allowing an attacker to call remap_file_pages() on an ashmem mapping to restore VM_MAYWRITE and subsequently gain write access to an ashmem region that was supposed to be read-only. Additionally, read-only ashmem fds allow ASHMEM_PIN/UNPIN operations so pages can be marked purgable even without write access.
proposal.affected_product: Android ashmem (kernel driver) and upstream Linux ashmem driver; specific versions not stated (reproducer works on upstream Linux master and a Pixel 2 at 2019-09-05 security patch level)
proposal.cwe_quote: However, it improperly stores the backing shmem file, whose ->mmap() handler does not enforce the same restrictions, in ->vm_file.

AV.quote: remap_file_pages(addr, size, 0, 0, 0) on an ashmem mapping allows an attacker to raise the VM_MAYWRITE bit, allowing the attacker to gain write access to the ashmem allocation's backing file via mprotect().

proposal.recommended_next_step: Backport a kernel fix that prevents storing the underlying shmem file in vma->vm_file (or ensure the file's ->mmap enforces the same prot_mask), and add a test covering remap_file_pages() on ashmem mappings; consider disabling remap_file_pages in seccomp for relevant processes if not needed.
